title: Explicit Capacity-Achieving Quantum LDPC Codes List Decodable in Near-linear Time
authors: William Gay, Fernando Granha Jeronimo, Abhi Shukul
abstract: In classical coding theory, the quest for explicit codes achieving list decoding capacity has been an important driving force. While random codes are easily shown to achieve capacity, an explicit construction was only discovered decades later in the seminal work [Guruswami and Rudra, STOC 2006]. In quantum coding theory, it is highly desirable that a code family be LDPC. While good quantum codes were known for decades, obtaining the additional LDPC property was elusive. In fact, only very recently that good quantum LDPC codes were discovered in a breakthrough work [Panteleev and Kalachev, STOC 2022].   In this context, a natural question is to ask for an explicit family of quantum codes achieving list decoding capacity while also possessing the important LDPC property. In this work, we provide (to the best of our knowledge) the first explicit constructions of quantum LDPC codes achieving list decoding capacity, namely, with a list decoding radius approaching the quantum Singleton bound with constant list sizes. Furthermore, we provide near-linear time (in the block-length) list decoding algorithms approaching capacity.   Our explicit code construction are based on expander graphs via the quantum analogue of Alon-Edmonds-Luby (AEL) amplification [Bergamaschi, Golowich and Gunn, STOC 2024], and this enables the important LDPC property. Our efficient list decoding algorithms are obtained by generalizing the classical expander-based weak-regularity list decoding algorithms [Srivastava and Tulsiani, FOCS 2025] [Jeronimo and Singh, 2025] to suitable instantiations of quantum AEL.
summary: This paper presents the first explicit construction of quantum LDPC codes that achieve list decoding capacity. The codes are built using expander graphs via quantum AEL amplification, and the authors develop a corresponding near-linear time decoding algorithm. This advances the field by providing highly structured, efficient quantum error-correcting codes.
main_problem: To construct explicit quantum Low-Density Parity-Check (LDPC) codes that achieve list decoding capacity and are decodable in near-linear time.
main_result: The authors provide the first explicit construction of such quantum LDPC codes, achieving a list decoding radius approaching the quantum Singleton bound with constant list sizes.
method: The construction utilizes expander graphs via the quantum analogue of Alon-Edmonds-Luby (AEL) amplification, and the decoding algorithm generalizes classical weak-regularity list decoding techniques.
model_or_system: The work operates in the framework of quantum error correction, specifically constructing CSS codes defined over finite fields, which are characterized by their LDPC structure.
key_observables: List decoding radius ($	au_N$), code rate ($R_N$), list size ($\ell$), and decoding time complexity.
important_parameters: Block length ($N$), list size ($\ell = O(1/\epsilon)$), and the required rate $R$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the existence of suitable expander graphs and the ability to solve local Constraint Satisfaction Problems (CSPs) efficiently.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general problem statement to the explicit construction using qAEL codes, followed by the development of a near-linear time decoding algorithm based on solving local CSPs and outer stitching.
why_interesting: This work pushes the boundaries of quantum error correction by combining the desirable LDPC structure with capacity-achieving list decoding guarantees, which is crucial for practical quantum computation.
